decision.explanation: The available evidence from the phase 2 trial (pmid-27283860) confirms that the combination of dabrafenib and trametinib demonstrates significant antitumor activity in patients with previously treated metastatic BRAF V600E-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Specifically, the investigator-assessed confirmed overall response rate was 63.2% (95% CI 49.3-75.6), which directly supports the claim that this therapy is associated with sensitivity/response in this molecularly defined population. The study population is defined by the presence of the BRAF V600E mutation, and the clinical outcome validates the predictive significance of this variant for response to the combination therapy. While specific molecular assay details and explicit somatic confirmation text are not provided in the source snippet, the clinical context and trial design support the somatic nature of the mutation in this metastatic setting. The claim is fully evidenced by the reported response rates.

citations.quote: In this phase 2, multicenter, nonrandomized, open-label study of patients with pretreated metastatic BRAF V600E-mutant NSCLC, antitumor activity and safety of oral dabrafenib (150 mg twice daily) plus oral trametinib (2 mg once daily) were evaluated. . . .
